ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 18980, December 31, 2021, as amended; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, Presidential Decree No. 32271; Real Name Financial Transactions Act, Act No. 9641; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Act No. 19304; Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Office, Seoul Central District Court, Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain certified copy from the issuing registry; submit to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for a single Apostille certificate; no consular legalization. Consular Legalization path for non-Apostille member states: certified copy from the registry; MOFA legalization; then legalization by the consulate of the destination state; no Apostille. Paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean Corporate Registration Extract showing current existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certified extract from the registry; Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; no consular step. Consular Legalization path for non-Apostille states: MOFA legalization followed by destination consulate legalization; never use Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Banking Mandate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public licensed by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarization before a Korean notary public; then Apostille by MOFA. Consular Legalization path: notarization before a Korean notary; then MOFA legalization; then legalization at the consulate of the receiving state. These two paths are strict alternatives and are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry Office or Notary Public in the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarized/certified copy; Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization path: notarized/certified copy; MOFA legalization; destination consulate legalization. No document may receive both an Apostille and a consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate banking branch of a licensed Korean commercial bank (e.g., Shinhan, Kookmin, Woori, or Hana)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: bank officer signature notarized; Apostille by MOFA. Consular Legalization path: signature notarized; MOFA legalization; destination consulate legalization. The two authentication frameworks are parallel and mutually exclusive; sequential chaining is prohibited.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories must be screened against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit designated persons list, the Financial Services Commission PEP database, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and sanctions adopted under Korean domestic law. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons, including foreign and domestic PEPs. Negative news, source of wealth, source of funds, passport, nationality, date of birth, address, and relationship to the Ro-Ro shipping entity must be documented. Screening results must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends, and transaction monitoring must cover wire transfer and SWIFT LC payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registry Office (IROS, www.iros.go.kr) Commercial Name Clearance Portal operated by the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Korean script (Hangul); foreign-origin names may be transliterated phonetically into Hangul and must be submitted with a precise romanization equivalence. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive subject/trademark element, (2) a business purpose descriptor such as ocean transport or automotive carrier service, (3) a commercial company indicator, and (4) the statutory legal form suffix Chusik Hoesa. The proposed name cannot be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in the national commercial registry database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the name, the applicant may file a written objection with the court registrar within 14 days, attaching the rejection notice, revised Hangul name, and a memorandum showing non-identical pronunciation and no confusion with existing registrations. The registrar must re-screen the name under the Commercial Act. If the objection is again rejected, the applicant may request adjudication from the district court and then appeal under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days. The name reservation does not automatically extend during appeal, so counsel should reserve an alternative name immediately.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox without a dedicated physical suite is not permissible as the registered office for a deep-sea Ro-Ro carrier because the Commercial Act requires an actual place of management, the local tax office will reject such an address for VAT and corporate tax domicile, and Korean banks require a physical branch visit and evidence of operational substance before opening corporate accounts or issuing Swift LC facilities. A serviced office with a dedicated lease, management suite, employee presence, and transparent disclosure to the shipping regulator may be accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: 1. lease contract in the company name; 2. exterior signage at the registered address; 3. dedicated office furniture and computer equipment; 4. at least one officer or employee physically present during business hours; 5. vessel chartering records and financial books available at the address; 6. corporate seal and bank correspondence maintained at the office. Quantified risk: approximately 28% probability of an unannounced inspection during the first 12 months after registration for a newly licensed ocean carrier, declining to approximately 12% after substantial commercial substance is demonstrated.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as revised by Act No. 19084 (2022)); incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) is governed by Articles 288 through 331; corporate governance and auditing by Articles 361 through 409; share subscription deposit requirement at Article 294; and corporate registration procedure under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Office (Corporate Registration Division) under the Supreme Court of Korea; territorial jurisdiction lies with the district court registry of the principal registered office, commonly the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office for Seoul-based companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation plus the Statutory Corporation Registration Application (Company Incorporation Registration) including the register of directors, auditor, and corporate seal certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a private Chusik Hoesa under the current Commercial Act. The company may be formed with as little as KRW 1, but the full subscription price of the allotted shares must be deposited into a blocked escrow account at a bank in the name of the company to satisfy Article 294. The bank certificate of deposit must accompany the registration application; escrow is released automatically upon issuance of the registration certificate. For an ocean car-carrier operation, banks and chartering counterparties will generally require materially higher paid-in capital and net worth sufficient for vessel casualty, war risks, and contractual liabilities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME CHUSIK HOESA] - A stock corporation organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea for deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle carrier services (ISIC 5012). The first meeting of the Board of Directors was duly convened and held on [Date], at the registered office located in [City], Republic of Korea. Each initial director received lawful notice; the directors present constituted a quorum. The meeting was chaired by the oldest director present. After due deliberation, the following resolutions were adopted unanimously. WHEREAS, the Company has been incorporated through the initial Articles of Incorporation authorizing an aggregate share capital of [KRW X] divided into [Y] fully paid ordinary shares; WHEREAS, each promoter and subscriber has paid in full the subscription price into a designated blocked bank account at [Bank], and the bank certificate of deposit has been submitted to the registry; WHEREAS, the Company must designate its registered office, approve banking institutions, and appoint its statutory officers before transacting business; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. Capital Subscription and Share Allocation. The Board ratifies the share subscription ledger, confirms that the entire authorized capital has been fully paid by the subscribers, and authorizes issuance of the allotted ordinary shares to the shareholders of record. 2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [full address]; the Representative Director shall file the registration and give notice to tax authorities under the Registered Office provisions. 3. Banking Authorization. The Company shall open corporate accounts at [Bank] and at one or more licensed foreign exchange banks to receive Swift L/C, electronic transfer, freight collections, and working capital deposits. Banking affairs will be managed by the Chief Executive Officer together with one other designated officer for amounts above [threshold]. 4. Statutory Officers. [Director A] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [Director B] is appointed Chief Operating Officer, and [Auditor C] is appointed statutory Auditor in accordance with the Commercial Act. All officers are granted full powers to execute contracts, charterparties, bills of lading, permits and insurance instruments. 5. Implementation. The Representative Director is directed, authorized and empowered to execute any and all applications, representations, signatures, notices, and contracts required to complete corporation registration, maritime licensing, ship registration, environmental compliance, employer and civil defense registrations, and banking formalities in order to commence ocean Ro-Ro vehicle transport operations. The Board ratified all lawful acts performed by the officers and promoters prior to this resolution. This resolution is effective immediately, shall be recorded in the official minutes, and a certified copy shall be retained at the registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry Office (Corporate Registration Division) of the competent local district court; online electronic filing through the Supreme Court Registry system at www.iros.go.kr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration through the electronic filing portal of the Court Registry Office or in person. Before filing, have the Articles of Incorporation notarized by a South Korean notary public in the name of the promoters, collect all subscription deposits into a blocked escrow account, and adopt the First Board Resolution. The filing must include the paid-up capital verification certificate from the escrow bank, the notarized articles, and the completed form registering directors and auditor. Submit to the territorial district court; the registration officer verifies the statutory due process. Payment of the official registration fee and stamp tax must be made before the application is accepted. After approval, the court issues the certificate of corporate registration and a certified copy of the registration register, which constitutes the company's formation in law.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription plan and allocation ledger
Bank certificate evidencing full paid-in capital deposit in blocked escrow account
First Board Resolution adopting registered office, officers, and banking authorization
Corporate seal declaration and seal certificate application
Power of attorney for local counsel or filing agent, if any
Foreign investment report confirmation for non-resident shareholders, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a request for correction or a suspension order, submit the missing notarized articles, capital deposit certificate, or officer consent forms within the statutory correction period, normally ten days. If registration is refused, file an immediate appeal with the competent district court and simultaneously cure the noted deficiency; legal counsel should be engaged to avoid repeat filings. Registration fees, if forfeited, are not automatically refunded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Business Registration at National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax Service portal (www.hometax.go.kr); district tax office with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the certified certificate of incorporation and the company seal certificate to the jurisdictional tax office or submit through HomeTax Service. The application for business registration must be filed within 30 days of incorporation and before any taxable transaction is made. Indicate ISIC 5012 and the expected Ro-Ro shipping revenue; attach the lease agreement for the registered office and the representative director's identification. The district tax office issues a corporate business registration certificate and assigns a registered business identification number; notify banks and counterparties after receipt. For foreign investors, attach the foreign investment report confirmation from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, if applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified certificate of corporation registration
Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Rental contract or title deed for registered office
Representative director's identification document
Company seal certificate
Foreign investment confirmation certificate, if foreign-owned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the submission, respond through HomeTax Service within 15 days by uploading the corrected lease agreement, financial statement, or power of attorney. If business registration is refused, request reconsideration from the district tax office, then file an appeal to the Tax Tribunal; continuing business before issuance may generate tax penalties, so all shipment and billing operations should await issuance of the Business Registration Certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate and Foreign Exchange Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank and authorized foreign exchange bank in the Republic of Korea; compliance and AML division of the institution acting as the corporate banker.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate foreign-exchange bank account at an authorized Korean commercial bank. Present the certified incorporation certificate, business registration certificate, original corporate seal and officer seal certificate, representative director passport, and Articles of Incorporation. The bank will conduct customer due diligence in accordance with the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and anti-money laundering regulations. Because the company will collect freight payments through Swift L/C and wire transfers, apply for a foreign exchange transfer purpose code and obtain the foreign exchange bank custody seal. The bank's compliance officer may require ultimate beneficial owner declarations; account activation is conditional on passing clearance and on the deposit or wiring of initial capital funds.
required_dossiers: Certified incorporation certificate
Business registration certificate
Corporate seal certificate
Authorized officer identification documents
Foreign exchange bank seal application, if required
AML/KYC and ultimate beneficial owner declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application for incomplete AML documentation, resubmit with a complete UBO declaration, verified shareholder register, and sworn source-of-funds statement. The applicant may alternatively select another licensed bank; any unlawful refusal by a bank may be reported to the Financial Supervisory Service, but in ordinary practice the deficiency is cured within the SLA period by submission of a clean compliance package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime Operating License, Ship Registration, and Safety Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF); Korea Maritime Transportation Safety Authority (KOMSA); local Ship Registry Office under MOF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the international cargo transport business license at the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries under the Marine Transportation Act. Submit the corporate registration certificate, business plan containing the proposed Ro-Ro trade routes and vessel acquisition plans, proof of ownership or long-term charter for at least one vessel suitable for car carrier transport, and financial solvency documents. The MOF will review national maritime policy, route adequacy, safety management capability, and financial fitness. After approval, register the vessel at the local Ship Registry Office and obtain the Vessel Safety Certificate and International Load Line Certificate through the Korea Maritime Transportation Safety Authority. The licensing authority may require a Safety Management Certificate under the ISM Code. Operation may begin only after all licenses, vessel certificates, and manning documents are in place.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate
Business registration certificate
Articles of Incorporation and First Board Resolution
Detailed business plan for Ro-Ro shipping routes
Vessel ownership deed or long-term charter contract
Vessel classification, flag, and tonnage particulars
Financial statements or bank guarantee for maritime liability
Crew licenses, ISM Safety Management Certificate, and insurance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOF qualifies the application or requests revised documents, submit the supplementary route analysis, charterparty, and financial statements within the prescribed remand period. If the license is refused, file for administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeals Act with MOF and then seek judicial review in the Administrative Court; in parallel, pursue a large-charterer guarantee to satisfy financial solvency. Vessel registration deficiencies may be cured by obtaining missing survey certificates from KOMSA before reapplying.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF); Korea Maritime Transportation Safety Authority (KOMSA); local port and municipal authority for onshore Ro-Ro handling facilities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Cargo Transport Business License (Permit) under the Marine Transportation Act of Korea, together with vessel registration under the Vessel Act and Vessel Safety Act certificates for a deep-sea Ro-Ro car carrier.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable to land-based manufacturing EIA; marine environmental regulatory authority is the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries under the Marine Environment Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act for pure vessel operations because no new stationary facility is created. However, an Environmental Registration and Marine Area Utilization Consultation may be required if the operator constructs or materially alters port quays, berths, onshore vehicle storage yards, or fixed marine terminals associated with the Ro-Ro service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Vessels must comply with MARPOL 73/78 Annex VI sulfur cap of 0.50 percent m/m fuel sulfur content or equivalent scrubber technology; Annexes I, II, IV and V discharge controls; Ballast Water Management Convention D-2 standard; and domestic Marine Environment Management Act restricted discharge standards for wastewater, bilge, garbage, and hazardous substances. Wet and dry cargo residues must be discharged only through licensed marine waste handling facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Onshore registered offices, port cabins, and vehicle storage buildings require a Fire Protection Certificate and Civil Defense inspection clearance from the local fire department under the Fire Services Act. Vessels require KOMSA ship surveys for fire safety per SOLAS and the Vessel Safety Act, inspections for load lines and stability, and a Safety Management Certificate under the ISM Code. Occupational workplace safety for shore crews and cargo handlers requires KOSHA risk assessments, lashing and cargo-securing work plans, and incident reporting under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) for business registration, VAT e-invoices, VAT returns, and entity tax filings; Korea Customs Service (KCS) through UNIPASS (unipass.customs.go.kr) for export/import declarations and export confirmation certificates.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean-incorporated Chusik Hoesa, the foreign non-resident shareholders first complete the commercial company registration at the competent Korean court under the Commercial Act. The entity must then register for Korean tax at the NTSelectronic HomeTax system by submitting the corporate tax inception registration and the VAT business registration application within 20 days of commencement of business, attaching the certificate of incorporation, court registration certificate, articles of incorporation, evidence of the registered business site, appointment of an authorized representative, and shareholder ownership/beneficial-ownership declarations. A foreign investor is permitted 100% ownership without minimum capital; the court registry does not require Korean nationality for directors. NTS assigns a single 10-digit Business Registration Number that is the unified tax identification number for corporate income tax, VAT withholding, employer withholding, and customs usage. A foreign non-resident entity that has a Korean place of business must separately complete NTS non-resident business registration through HomeTax using apostilled/certified foreign incorporation documents, foreign tax identification number, appointment of a Korean tax representative, and a domestic address for service. A foreign entity without any Korean domestic place of business is not entitled to a general Korean VAT registration number; it is required to register only in the specific non-resident simplified VAT regime if it supplies enumerated digital services to Korean non-taxable consumers, and otherwise it simply files from its foreign tax identity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None comparable to a U.S. check-the-box election. Every Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily treated as a separate resident corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income, with no pass-through or partnership election available. The only material statutory election is the consolidated corporate tax return regime available under the Corporate Tax Act, which a domestic parent and its wholly-owned Korean subsidiaries may elect upon NTS approval. Korea also applies mandatory hybrid-mismatch deduction adjustment rules; these are not elective and do not permit a taxpayer to reclassify the Chusik Hoesa.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 - no general turnover threshold; every person, resident or non-resident with a domestic place of business, that supplies goods or services in the course of business in Korea is required to register for VAT with NTS. The simplified taxable person regime for certain small merchants does not remove the registration obligation, is subject to an annual revenue threshold, and is unavailable to a corporate deep-sea RoRo ocean carrier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoicing through the NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system. General taxable businesses must generate each VAT tax invoice with prescribed statutory content and transmit it to NTS by the day following the supply date; transmission may occur through HomeTax web, machine-to-machine API, or an NTS-authorized delegated e-invoice service provider. There is no physical fiscal-stamp clearance, but the NTS assigns an electronic integrity value to each transmitted record, and input VAT recovery generally depends on the counterparty retaining a properly transmitted electronic tax invoice. Export and zero-rated international shipping documentation is filed through KCS UNIPASS, which uses electronic EDI/XML messaging and exchanges export-clearance data with NTS. Zero-rated sales must be included in the VAT return under the zero-rated category, and underlying proof must be retained for statutory audit periods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT treatment is available for the export of goods and for international maritime transport, including deep-sea RoRo ocean vehicle transport, under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act. A Korean Chusik Hoesa can invoice international ocean freight at 0% only where the transport service is supplied in connection with carriage by a vessel engaged in international navigation, the voyage involves movement between Korean and foreign ports or between foreign ports, the customer is a foreign person, and the freight revenue is earned in and payable in a foreign currency. The zero rate does not apply to domestic cabotage or domestic port-to-port RoRo movements. The taxable person must hold contemporaneous evidence showing the foreign character of the voyage, the vehicles carried across customs borders or internationally, the issue of a commercial invoice and e-tax invoice to the foreign customer, and eventual settlement in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration and Export Declaration Certificate issued through Korea Customs Service UNIPASS for the vehicles exported on the RoRo voyage, reflecting the vessel identifier, cargo type, port of loading, foreign port of discharge, shipper, and consignee
Vessel's Bill of Lading or sea waybill issued in the carrier's name for the international RoRo voyage, evidencing loading at the origin port and discharge at the foreign destination port
Charter party agreement, voyage charter, slot charter, or contract of affreightment for the ocean transport, together with the commercial freight invoice issued to the foreign customer
VAT e-Tax Invoice issued to the foreign customer through HomeTax with the zero-rated tax code and a clear description of international sea transportation of vehicles

Foreign exchange receipt certificate or bank settlement confirmation issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, evidencing receipt of the ocean freight from abroad in a convertible currency
Vehicle stowage plan and cargo manifest reconciled to the bills of lading and the customs export declaration, showing vehicle count, identifying numbers, ports, and vessel voyage details
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS, together with Korea Customs Service and the Foreign Exchange Information System, audits zero-rating claims by matching export declarations, e-Tax Invoices, bills of lading, cargo manifests, charter parties, and foreign exchange settlement records. If any required document is missing, forged, inconsistent, dated outside the statutory repatriation period, or unsupported by actual foreign-currency repatriation, NTS will disallow the zero rate, retroactively assess 10% VAT on the gross freight, and impose statutory underreporting and non-payment additional tax plus interest. Deliberate issuance of false tax invoices, fraudulent export documentation, or misclassification of domestic carriage as international transport may result in criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including fines and imprisonment. Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, the assessment and clawback period is extended to at least 10 years in cases of false or fraudulent returns, and failure to obtain an authorized extension for late repatriation of export proceeds is separately penalized under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with possible loss of export confirmation status and zero-rating entitlement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK); FX policy and licensing are co-administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a free-floating Korean won and a generally convertible current-account regime regulated by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Inbound and outbound current payments such as trade freight settlement, port disbursements, vessel tonnage fees and dividend remittances are classified as current transactions and may be executed without a license, provided the underlying commercial documentation is submitted to the designated foreign-exchange bank. Capital-account movements, however, are not freely convertible: the initial equity contribution into a Chusik Hoesa must be pre-notified under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA), obtain a KOTRA/Invest Korea registration number, and be booked into an FDI escrow account at a licensed bank before the won can be deployed. Profit remittance by a foreign shareholder is legally permitted but operationally conditioned on the payment of Korean corporate tax withholding clearance, submission of audited financial statements, and evidence that the dividend was properly approved by the shareholders general meeting. There are no residual surrender requirements for export earnings; the exporter may retain foreign currency in a designated account, but any conversion to won must be settled at the prevailing market rate through a licensed bank. The practical treasury hurdle is therefore documentary traceability and transaction purpose validation, not exchange rationing, and the company must present a full real-transaction evidence file to move capital across accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export freight receivables and vehicle transport proceeds must be collected within six months from the date of the export declaration or invoice issue; if collection is delayed, the company must file a delay report with the designated foreign-exchange bank. The mandatory conversion ratio to Korean won is 0%; there is no forced surrender to the Bank of Korea. The foreign currency may be credited to a company foreign-currency account. If the treasury elects to convert the proceeds to KRW, the transaction is executed at the interbank market rate and the receipt is reported by the bank to the Korea Customs Service and the Electronic Trade Settlement System on the same business day.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Trade Settlement and Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI banking is not viable for a Korean Chusik Hoesa under the current legal framework. South Korea does not recognize offshore EMI licenses as equivalent to a banking license for resident corporations, and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act mandates that foreign-exchange business, inbound FDI settlement, and SWIFT settlement involving the Korean entity must pass through a licensed foreign-exchange bank. Offshore EMIs, including Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer and Currencycloud, may not hold the entitys KRW treasury balance, issue an IBAN, or execute MT103 settlement as principal. They can only serve as unlicensed quote-aggregation or payment-notification layers, with no legal capacity to handle the companys Korea-resident current-account payments. Practical feasibility rating: Low, and the treasury blueprint should default to domestic Tier-1 banks for all material cash flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance by at least one statutory director or the CFO/company secretary with an explicit board authority is mandatory for initial corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for a deep-sea Ro-Ro shipping company because the bank must capture real-name verification under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions. If the director is outside Korea, the bank will require the appointment of an in-country legal attorney or an officer who attends the Korean branch; some banking groups permit a limited video interview via a certified non-face-to-face onboarding system, but this is only accepted as an add-on, never as a substitute, for shipping and FIPA-regulated entities. The authorized natural person must present a notarized and apostilled certificate of appointment, the corporate seal, the entity certificate of incorporation, and the full UBO declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border UBO chain with opaque equity ownership in two or more maritime jurisdictions, such as a Marshall Islands flag vehicle or a Liberian holding company above the Korean entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry excerpts from the relevant company registry, complete shareholder register, UBO declaration, certificate of no bearer shares, a schematic ownership map notarized by a Korean notary, passports of all natural-person UBOs, and a signed Qualified UBO declaration prepared for the bank compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hits on the Ro-Ro vessel schedule due to port calls, cargo counterparties, bunker suppliers or vessel flag registries in or linked to OFAC, EU, UN or Korea-designated jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A current sanctions-screening report from a reputable compliance provider covering all vessels by IMO number, flag state and commercial operators; a complete charter-party compliance clause library; vessel voyage logs; war-risk and international restriction attestations from the maritime commercial manager; and an undertaking letter confirming that no payments are routed to sanctioned counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound equity injection from a non-resident shareholder whose wealth provenance is not documented, especially if funded via unlicensed payment channels or cryptocurrency intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth dossier including the shareholder's audited financial statements for the last three years, personal and corporate tax residency certificates, bank reference letters from an overseas correspondent bank, the executed FIPA/KOTRA FDI notification certificate, the investment business plan, funding trail bank statements, and a sworn affidavit confirming the origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-payment mismatch and invoice-value anomalies in disbursements to ports, stevedores, tug operators or offshore vessel-management companies that cannot be traced to the approved operational budget.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Charter party or freight service agreement, minutes of the board of directors approving each payment type, itemized port disbursement accounts, bunker supplier invoices, vessel classification or tonnage documents, the company treasury policy, and a projected cash-flow model showing each payment against an approved voyage.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity for the Chusik Hoesa must route as a foreign direct investment via SWIFT MT103 through a licensed designated foreign-exchange bank, with the FIPA notification number in SWIFT field 70 and the bank entering the transaction under the inward direct-investment equity settlement purpose code in the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System. The remittance must enter the FDI capital escrow account, after which the bank issues a Foreign Exchange Purchase/Deposit certificate. That certificate, accompanied by the FIPA registration certificate and board resolutions, is presented to the statutory external auditor for capital verification. The escrowed funds may not be withdrawn for the company operating account until the capital verification is complete, the dollar-for-won conversion is recorded at the ruling market rate, and the bank compliance team confirms the beneficial owner matches the notified FIPA investor list.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outgoing disbursements for Ro-Ro shipping operations should use SWIFT MT103 for port costs, agent fees, bunker settlement, crew payment, canal tolls and repair disbursements, with each payment supported by an approved disbursement order and a board-approved treasury schedule. For high-value capital purchases such as vessel acquisition or major retrofits, the company should activate a Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 using SWIFT MT700/MT798, with shipping documents as collateral. Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) are operationally permissible for lower-risk charter-related invoices, but the bank will require the presentation of charter party summaries, whatfage and stevedoring receipts, and underlying purchase orders to satisfy trade purpose verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards (USD/KRW, EUR/KRW, JPY/KRW) for freight collect, charter hire, bunker cost and port disbursement exposure
FX swaps for short-tenor liquidity conversion between Korean won and USD across the daily netting position
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) strictly aligned to the underlying foreign-currency vessel financing debt service

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on KRW only when the underlying receivable or payable is foreign-currency denominated and the hedging counterparty is an offshore institution, limited to real-demand tenors and subject to prior bank approval
Zero-premium structured currency collars as a risk-hedging overlay for bunker price and FX volatility, with prohibition on speculative naked positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting and approval of balance sheet, income statement, and statutory auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders (internal governance; no government filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No administrative strike-off in Korea; directors failing to prepare or present financial statements are subject to administrative fines up to KRW 5 million per violation, and unresolved deadlock may lead to a court-ordered meeting or involuntary winding-up at shareholders' request.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (juridical person tax) with approved financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the fiscal year-end for a 31 December year; if the company is subject to external audit, the deadline is automatically extended to 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or under-reporting incurs a 20% negligence penalty on unpaid tax and a daily late-payment surcharge approximately 0.03%; prolonged non-payment triggers asset seizure (including vessels), business registration revocation, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax (local surtax) return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent municipal or provincial tax authorities of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the corporate tax return deadline; 30 April for calendar-year filers, 31 May for externally audited companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a 20% negligence penalty on unpaid local tax plus daily late-payment interest; continued failure can lead to local tax seizure and enforcement sale of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report deliverable and filing (where mandatory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) via Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) electronic system plus Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) for auditor reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the annual shareholders' meeting (by 31 March for calendar-year companies); the auditor must file the final audit report with the FSC and KICPA within 2 weeks after the audit completion date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If no external audit is performed when required, the company and auditor can be fined up to KRW 50 million; directors may be subject to imprisonment up to 5 years for submitting false audit statements; failure to file an audit report does not lead to administrative strike-off but triggers regulatory sanctions and tax examination.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise annual business report (applicable when foreign ownership exists)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or a designated receiving bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the close of the business year; for a 31 December year, by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit may cause cancellation of the foreign-invested enterprise registration, loss of tax exemption or repatriation benefits, and an administrative fine under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act of up to KRW 3 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual Value Added Tax (VAT) returns and payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) Regional Tax Office / HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 for July-December taxable period; July 25 for January-June taxable period for calendar-year standard periods; monthly filers are due by the 25th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or under-payment triggers a 20% negligence penalty on unpaid VAT, a 10% penalty on proper tax amounts, and a daily late-payment surcharge; overdue VAT may result in business registration revocation and asset seizure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Korea's Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa must obtain a mandatory external audit by a licensed CPA if total assets at the fiscal year-end equal at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million). Listed companies are always audited. There is no separate turnover or headcount trigger for ordinary non-listed stock companies; however, the FSC may designate certain unlisted companies for audit on public-interest grounds, and companies with total assets of KRW 500 billion or more are treated as large unlisted corporations and must appoint an audit committee and designated auditor. The balance-sheet test predominates; turnover and headcount are only supplementary indicators for voluntary assurance, not statutory audit triggers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is required for listed companies and for designated non-listed financial institutions; non-listed companies may prepare financial statements under K-GAAP / KAS-NLC (Korean Accounting Standards for Non-Listed Companies). All compulsory audits are performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which are aligned with International Standards on Auditing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not require an annual UBO confirmation return for a private Chusik Hoesa, but the shareholder register must be updated continuously. Share transfers only become effective against the company when the transferee's name, address and shareholding are entered into the register of shareholders; therefore the company must effect every transfer promptly, treating any request within 30 days as the statutory 30-day reporting window for foreign investment changes. If the enterprise has foreign investors, any ownership change triggers a 30-day report to MOTIE/KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The company should also verify UBO details at each record date (usually 31 December) and before each ordinary general meeting. Failure to maintain the register subjects the responsible director to administrative fines under the Commercial Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder register) covering issued shares, paid-in amount, transfer dates and pledge or security entries
Register of Directors (internal director and senior officer roster with term, address and sanctions history; maintained alongside court commercial registration records)
Register of Charges/Mortgages (share pledge records appear in the holder register and pledge register; a mortgage or charge ledger must be kept if any secured interests exist)
Minute Book recording all shareholders' meetings, board of directors' meetings and audit committee or statutory auditor resolutions
Accounting books and vouchers including journal, ledgers, financial statements, business reports and audit reports

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 - USD 3,000 per year (KRW 1.3 million - 3.9 million) for a registered office / corporate secretary agent in Seoul or Busan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 20,000 - USD 80,000 for an ocean Ro-Ro carrier above the mandatory audit threshold; USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 for a smaller voluntary-audit shipping entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national top marginal rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surcharge resulting in 26.4% aggregate top marginal rate; lower brackets are 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, each subject to a 10% local surtax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible international ocean-going Ro-Ro shipping income may elect the Korean tonnage tax system under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, which substitutes the normal corporate income tax profit-base with a deemed tonnage-based profit per vessel net ton per day for eligible foreign-going vessels, substantially reducing effective taxation. R&D and facility investment tax credits are available for vessel construction and port automation; pre-construction liquidation and free trade zone port incentives apply mainly to customs/VAT rather than CIT. Foreign-source tramp or Ro-Ro revenue may also benefit from foreign tax credit relief and ocean-going shipping reserve mechanisms, while patent box/R&D super-deductions are not typically available for shipping operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return Form 1 (Calculation of Tax Base and Corporate Tax) under the Corporate Tax Act and Framework Act on Corporate Taxation, filed through the Korean National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr); attachments include audited IFRS/K-GAAP financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, related-party international transaction schedules, and vessel asset/depreciation registers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (by March 31 for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa), with a one-month extension available for audited or foreign-parented companies; quarterly advance corporate tax payments are required during the fiscal year for taxable base above prescribed thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identity, business registration number, entity name (Chusik Hoesa), headquarters address, representative director, fiscal year-end, and Korean Standard Industrial Classification code for deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle transport.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Korean business registration number and place of effective management. A Chusik Hoesa incorporated under the Korean Commercial Act is conclusively treated as a Korean tax resident and must file this return even if all overseas vessels are flagged under a foreign registry or foreign shareholders hold beneficial ownership; disclose the ultimate foreign beneficial owners in supplementary shareholder schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements and accounting method: attached income statement, statement of financial position, statement of comprehensive income, cash flow statement, and disclosure notes prepared under IFRS/K-GAAP; RoRo vessel costs capitalized as depreciation schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain Korean books separate from foreign chartering-agent books. Non-resident shipowners do not file Form 1; however, the Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa must include worldwide RoRo freight, vehicle-stowage, demurrage, and vessel charter income. Allocate voyage expenses between Korean-source and foreign-source gross income with contemporaneous voyage records and port-call dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation: book net income before tax is adjusted by temporary and permanent differences (depreciation on vessel hulls, provisions, entertainment disallowances, non-taxable income, overseas tax adjustments) to derive taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border RoRo shipping, apply consistent revenue recognition between bill of lading and completion-of-voyage method. Korean-source revenue accrues where loading, discharge, or intra-Korean RoRo move occurs; artificial loading of revenue or voyage expense into a foreign intercompany ship manager is prohibited and must be adjusted under the Framework Act on International Tax Affairs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base calculation and national corporate income tax rate computation after applying loss carryforwards, non-taxable income, and income deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Large RoRo operators compute the progressive 24% national rate and 10% local surtax at Box 4. If the tonnage tax election is made, enter the deemed tonnage profit in the international shipping tonnage tax schedule; the election is irrevocable for at least five years and is limited to eligible foreign-going ships.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income and total tax amount: national CIT plus local surtax, credits for R&D/facility investment, advance tax payments, withholding credits, and net tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends payable to non-resident shareholders are not deductible in Box 5 and the paying Chusik Hoesa must gross-up or withhold at remittance. Treaty reduction of the 22% aggregate dividend WHT is not granted as a Box 5 credit; it must be claimed separately through the withholding/dta relief procedure before remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income tax credit and foreign source income: foreign-source RoRo revenue, foreign tax paid, per-country foreign tax credit limitation, and any foreign branch profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa cannot claim the treaty Article 8 shipping-exemption for its own Korean-source income; the exemption analysis applies only to non-resident shareholders or foreign vessel owners treaty-resident in a relevant contracting state. Claim foreign tax credit with original foreign tax returns and translated receipts in each port-State jurisdiction where the vessel pays income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party international transaction disclosure schedule: controlled transactions with foreign related parties, transfer pricing methodology, arm's length range, and documentation readiness.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose intercompany time charters, voyage charters, slot charters, management fees, technical fees, and head-office cost allocations with non-resident affiliates. Local File preparation is compulsory when controlled cross-border transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; Master File preparation is compulsory when group scross-border transactions exceed KRW 100 billion; an annual report on international transactions is due with the corporate return once any single related counterparty transaction exceeds KRW 100 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payments to non-residents and withholding tax reconciliation: dividends, interest, royalties, charter hire, demurrage, commissions, and remittance schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare every outward remittance to a non-resident payee and calculate statutory 20% national WHT plus 2% local surtax unless the applicable DTA reduces the rate. For a RoRo vessel, charter hire or slot hire paid to a non-resident can be Korean-source when the freight is loaded or discharged in Korea; document effective control of the vessel and whether the recipient is a mere conduit to prevent denial of the shipping Article.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax schedule: 10% local surtax computation on the national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When withholding on a non-resident payee, remit 2% local surtax computed on the 20% statutory WHT base; combined reporting to HomeTax shows the aggregate 22% statutory burden. A non-resident's later treaty claim for refund/reduction must be filed with the same district office before or at the time of withholding remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and special regimes: employment credit, seafarer employment credit, investment credit for ship construction, and overseas market expansion activities, along with any free-zone or port-related incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-flag RoRo vessels may be ineligible for Korean vessel investment credits if the beneficial owner is a non-resident ship-leasing vehicle rather than the Korean Chusik Hoesa. Non-resident joint venture partners cannot claim Korean tax credits; only the Korean resident taxpayer that bears real vessel economic risk and operates the vessels through Korean decision-making may apply Box 10 credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Corporate Tax Return triggers a 10% additional tax on the unpaid tax; unfaithful/underreported returns incur a 20% surcharge; fraudulent returns with gross negligence incur a 40% surcharge; unpaid deferred tax accrues statutory daily delinquency interest of 0.025% per day, equivalent to about 9.125% annually. Where a Chusik Hoesa deliberately conceals Korean-source RoRo revenue or improperly shifts profit to a foreign shell, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act authorizes criminal referral, imprisonment up to 3 years, and a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax, and the National Tax Service may blacklist high-value tax evaders publicly and impose exit/travel bans on the representative director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national statutory dividend withholding tax on outbound dividends to non-resident shareholders, plus 2% local income tax surtax, producing a 22% aggregate statutory withholding rate; treaty-reduced rates are often 5% for a direct corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the voting capital and 10% for portfolio dividends under many Korean bilateral treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief before remittance, the Korean Chusik Hoesa must: (1) obtain from the non-resident recipient a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent foreign tax authority, dated within six months of the payment; (2) obtain a beneficial ownership certificate and a substantive-business declaration sufficient to rebut conduit and limitation-on-benefits clauses; (3) file the Korean tax treaty withholding application on HomeTax or with the competent district tax office upon which the reduced rate will be applied at the time of remittance; (4) retain the underlying vessel charter, board minutes, invoice trail, and UBO chain for at least five years; and (5) if the Korean office later finds the recipient lacks beneficial ownership, pay the full 22% deficiency with daily interest and penalties. Where a dividend is paid to a foreign entity resident in a tax treaty jurisdiction but lacking genuine economic activities, Korea may apply the anti-avoidance rule or principal-purposes test and deny treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory outbound interest and royalty withholding tax is 20% plus 2% local surtax, aggregating 22% absent treaty reduction. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 10% and royalties to 10% or 15% depending on the counterparty country; royalty characterization of software, technical service, or vessel flag license fees must align with the OECD Model Tax Convention commentary and Korean characterization precedent. RoRo shipping charter hire and freight are generally not royalties but may be taxed as shipping income; most Korean DTAs permit the foreign shipping enterprise to be exempt from Korean-source shipping tax when the foreign flag operator is a resident of the treaty jurisdiction and effective management is outside Korea.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is mandatory when the total amount of cross-border controlled transactions between the Korean Chusik Hoesa and foreign related parties exceeds KRW 5 billion during the fiscal year; Master File documentation is mandatory when the multinational group's total cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 100 billion. An annual international transaction report is filed on HomeTax with the corporate return once controlled cross-border transactions with any single foreign related party exceed KRW 100 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not administer the offshore-centre Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) label, but the substance-over-form doctrine under Article 96-2 of the Framework Act on International Tax Affairs and the limitation-on-benefits provisions of each DTA impose a mandatory Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) analysis. The Korean Chusik Hoesa must own or time-charter the RoRo vessels, employ the master commercial and crewing decision, negotiate bunker and port contracts, control voyage planning and risk, and keep strategic vessel operation management in Korea. If the NTS finds that the foreign shareholder is a shell or that the Korean entity is a letter-box operating only through non-resident decision-makers, the authorities may recharacterize the structure, deny treaty benefits, disallow foreign tax credit, impose transfer pricing adjustments, and apply penalties under domestic anti-avoidance rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion by Falsifying RoRo Revenue and Voyage Accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately suppressing bill-of-lading revenue, understating the number of loaded motor vehicles, artificially moving Korean-port revenue to a foreign related vessel operator, falsifying ballast-bonus or demurrage invoices, or mischaracterizing Korean freight income as foreign-source income on the corporate tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 prescribes imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to 5 times the evaded tax for unlawful evasion. National Tax Collection Act surcharges apply at 40% for fraudulent underreporting plus daily overdue interest at 0.025%; the National Tax Service may publicly disclose the Chusik Hoesa as a high-value tax evader and refer the representative director to the prosecutor's office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil where the Chusik Hoesa is undercapitalized or directed fraudulently, making the representative director jointly liable for unpaid CIT, surcharges, and interest. The director's personal bank accounts, vessel shares, and real property can be seized without benefit of limitation of liability; a travel ban is imposed by the Korean Immigration Service for unpaid national taxes exceeding the statutory threshold; deliberate tax evasion over the criminal threshold carries imprisonment and confiscation of personally held vessel proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold or Remit Non-Resident Withholding Tax on Outbound Dividends, Interest, Royalties, and Ship Charters
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or paying interest, royalties, management fees, or RoRo charter hire to a non-resident parent or related foreign entity without withholding the statutory 22% aggregate WHT, filing a false withholding return, failing to remit withheld amounts, or applying a treaty rate without a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership substantiation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act withholding rules render the Chusik Hoesa liable for the unwithheld or un-remitted tax plus an additional 10% collection penalty on the unpaid withholding amount and daily delinquency interest. A false withholding statement is a criminal violation of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to 5 times the under-withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director is jointly and severally liable with the company for withheld but un-remitted taxes because a withholding agent is a statutory fiduciary of collected taxes; the NTS can seize director assets without seeking judgment against the corporate entity first. The director is subject to a domestic and overseas travel ban, disqualification from government contract privileges, and criminal imprisonment if the failure was intentional or accompanied by a fabricated remittance payment confirmation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing, Thin Capitalization, and Shell-Company Substance Infringement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the Korean Chusik Hoesa so that intercompany RoRo operating profits are shifted to a zero-tax Marshall Islands or Hong Kong subsidiary through excessive charter-hire fees, slot-purchase fees, technical royalties, or management fees; failing to prepare Local File/Master File when statutory thresholds are met; failing to file the annual international transaction report; or maintaining only a nominal Korean head office while central management and decision-making is performed abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Framework Act on International Tax Affairs authorizes the NTS to compute an arm's length taxable income and imposes an international tax adjustment penalty of 10% of the adjusted amount, increased to 15% in fraud cases; failure to file the international transaction report carries a separate statutory fine; denial of treaty relief converts the outbound dividend/royalty to the full 22% withholding with interest; and the resulting deficiency triggers criminal referral when a false or deceptive TP document was used to conceal Korean-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve abusive intercompany rates or cause the Korean RoRo entity to be no more than a shell face piercing of the corporate veil and personal restitution of the adjusted tax, interest, and penalties. Korean courts and the NTS may impose joint liability on directors for causing the company to be undercapitalized or insolvent at the time of the tax adjustment; the director is blacklisted as a high-risk international tax evader, subjected to an immigration control travel ban, and, for intentional documentation fraud, sentenced to imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act where the concealed revenue or adjusted tax exceeds the statutory criminal threshold.
